md_description: This DAG represents a coral reef microbiome study in which microbial community samples from different depths and locations in the Great Barrier Reef are collected, prepared, and sequenced for 16S rRNA gene profiling. Concurrent field measurements of water temperature, pH, salinity, and nutrients are captured at each site. The resulting sequencing reads, microbial community feature table, and environmental measurements are processed and integrated to assess spatial heterogeneity, microbial diversity, community structure, and their potential relationship to coral health and resilience.

coral_reef_sample.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic identity and origin/provenance fields for the collected coral reef sample: what it is, where it was collected, and the sampling context needed to distinguish samples across the Great Barrier Reef. I excluded preservation, DNA extraction, sequencing, environmental sensor readings, and any downstream processing because those belong to Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating generic experiment identifiers or any fields that would overlap with downstream environmental table, raw reads, or amplicon features. Since no already_generated fields were provided, there were no explicit duplicates to avoid beyond staying within the Entity semantic scope.

md_schema.descr: Unique sample identifier for this collected reef microbial community sample; use a stable string such as 'GBR_D01_SITE03_S01'. Generated once at collection and used to link this entity to preservation, DNA extraction, and environmental capture steps.
Date the coral reef sample was collected in the field (YYYY-MM-DD); recorded at the point of sampling and used to anchor spatial/environmental comparisons.
Named reef location or site label within the Great Barrier Reef where the sample was collected; e.g. a reef name or station code.
Sampling latitude in decimal degrees at the collection point; typical range for the Great Barrier Reef is approximately -25 to -10. Measured or recorded at collection site.
Sampling longitude in decimal degrees at the collection point; typical range for the Great Barrier Reef is approximately 142 to 155. Measured or recorded at collection site.

Water depth in meters where the coral reef sample was collected; measured at the sampling point to capture depth-associated microbial variation, typically within the shallow reef to mesophotic range used in the study.

Physical material collected as the entity source; for this study the sample is a reef-associated microbial community sample. Use this to distinguish the sample material from later extracted DNA or preserved material.

Whether the sample was collected from a coral-associated reef environment or from surrounding reef seawater/substrate context. Use this only to describe the collected entity origin, not downstream measurements.

sample_preservation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only preservation workflow parameters and reagent/condition details that describe how the collected reef sample was stabilized for later DNA extraction. I excluded sample origin, collection location/depth, and any DNA yield or downstream library/sequencing properties because those belong to the upstream Entity or downstream Entity/Process nodes. I also did not repeat any sample identifier-type fields conceptually tied to the coral_reef_sample node. No already_generated list was provided, so there were no explicit field collisions to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Preservation approach applied immediately after collection to stabilize the reef sample before nucleic acid extraction; record the operational method used in this study, e.g. freezing, chemical preservative, or buffer-based stabilization.
Preservative reagent or medium used during sample stabilization, if applicable; report the reagent name and concentration or formulation when relevant, measured/assigned at the preservation step.

Temperature in degrees Celsius used during preservation or short-term storage immediately after collection; measure at the point the sample is placed into preservation and before DNA extraction. Typical values may include ambient field temperature, 4, -20, or -80 depending on workflow.
Elapsed time in minutes from collection to completion of stabilization/preservation handling; record this at the preservation step to indicate delay before downstream nucleic acid extraction.
Number of days the preserved sample was held in storage before DNA extraction; report the interval between preservation and extraction to support assessment of material stability.
Storage condition used after preservation and before extraction; specify the holding state of the sample, such as refrigerated, frozen, or ambient, as implemented in this workflow.
Free-text notes on any deviations, transport handling, or stabilization issues encountered during preservation of the collected reef sample; capture only process-relevant observations.

preserved_reef_sample.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the preserved material after stabilization, so I included intrinsic state and custody/provenance fields relevant to the preserved sample itself. I excluded collection-site details, preservation protocol parameters, and DNA extraction specifics because those belong to the upstream sample entity or the sample_preservation and dna_extraction processes. Since no already_generated list was provided, there were no explicit duplicate-field constraints beyond staying within the preserved-sample entity scope and not repeating the original sample identifier semantics.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the preserved coral reef sample entity; use a stable string such as 'GBR_D01_SITE03_S01_PRES'. This identifies the preserved material as distinct from the original field-collected sample while preserving linkage to it.
Current preservation state of the sample at the time it enters laboratory processing; record the final stabilized form used for extraction readiness.

Physical storage location for the preserved sample before DNA extraction, such as freezer, refrigerator, field cooler, or repository location; record the location at the time this entity is used downstream.
Storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the preserved sample immediately before DNA extraction; typical values may include 4, -20, or -80 depending on preservation workflow.

Qualitative assessment of the preserved sample condition prior to DNA extraction, based on visible leakage, thawing, degradation, or container compromise; record as an operational status for laboratory readiness.
Boolean flag indicating whether the preserved sample was deemed ready for downstream DNA extraction without additional stabilization or cleanup.

dna_extraction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only extraction workflow parameters, reagents, and process quality indicators that describe how DNA was obtained from the preserved reef sample. I excluded input sample provenance and downstream DNA concentration/purity entity properties because those belong to the preserved_reef_sample and community_dna entities. I also avoided sequencing-library or read-level details because those are downstream. No already_generated list was provided, so there were no explicit field collisions to avoid.

md_schema.descr: DNA extraction kit or protocol used to isolate microbial DNA from the preserved reef sample; report the kit name/model or validated extraction method used in this study.
Specific protocol variant or version applied during extraction, including any laboratory adaptation or manufacturer workflow version used at the extraction step.
Cell lysis approach used during extraction, such as bead beating, enzymatic lysis, chemical lysis, or combined methods; describe the operative extraction condition rather than sample properties.
Duration in minutes of the lysis phase during extraction; record the time spent actively disrupting cells before DNA recovery.
Final elution volume in microliters used to recover DNA from the extraction matrix; record the volume at the end of the extraction procedure.
Number of independent extraction replicates performed for this preserved reef sample; measure at the extraction step to document technical replication.

Total DNA yield in nanograms recovered from the extraction, measured at the end of the extraction workflow before downstream library preparation; typical values depend on biomass and protocol efficiency.
DNA purity ratio A260/A280 measured on the extracted material immediately after extraction; used as a technical quality indicator for downstream amplicon sequencing.
Batch or run identifier for the extraction workflow, used to track shared reagent lots or processing runs across samples; format example: 'EXT_BATCH_2024_05_01'.

community_dna.reasoning: I corrected the community_dna Entity schema by removing the colliding field dna_purity_a260_a280 because it was already generated earlier in the DAG and must not be repeated. I kept only non-duplicative intrinsic DNA entity fields that still describe the extracted material itself, such as identity, concentration, total mass, A260/A230 purity, fragment size, storage state, and quality flag. I excluded extraction-process details, library prep, and sequencing fields because they belong to other node types.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the extracted community DNA entity; use a stable string such as 'GBR_D01_SITE03_S01_DNA'. This identifies the DNA extract as distinct from the preserved sample and downstream sequencing library.

Measured concentration of extracted community DNA in nanograms per microliter, assessed after extraction and before library preparation; typical values may range from low trace amounts to tens of ng/µL depending on biomass and extraction efficiency.
Total mass of DNA recovered in nanograms from the extraction, calculated from concentration and elution volume or measured directly at the post-extraction assessment point.
Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A230 for the extracted DNA, measured after extraction and before library preparation to assess salt or organic carryover.

Approximate dominant DNA fragment size in base pairs for the extracted community DNA, assessed by gel or electrophoretic method after extraction and before amplification; useful for gauging suitability for amplicon library prep.
Storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the extracted DNA after extraction and prior to library preparation; commonly 4 or -20 depending on short-term handling.
Buffer or solvent in which the extracted DNA is stored before downstream use, such as nuclease-free water or TE buffer.
Operational quality assessment of the extracted DNA prior to library preparation, indicating whether the extract was suitable for downstream amplicon sequencing.

env_site_measurement.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration used to record on-site environmental conditions at the sampling site. I excluded the environmental values themselves as a Signal-node territory issue, because raw readings and file-level properties belong to env_signal, while processed summaries belong downstream to env_processing/environmental_table. I also avoided any sample identity fields already owned by the coral_reef_sample entity. No already_generated list was supplied, so the schema is limited by capture semantics and the DAG context rather than explicit field-name collisions.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the environmental measurement session at a sampling site; use a stable string such as 'ENV_GBR_SITE03_2024_05_17'. Assigned at the time of field measurement to link the capture setup to downstream raw environmental readings.
Name of the field sensor suite or combined instrumentation platform used to measure site conditions, such as multiparameter sonde or portable water-quality meter.
Manufacturer of the environmental field instrument used for capture, recorded as the hardware vendor responsible for the deployed sensor suite.
Model designation of the environmental instrument used for capture, recorded at measurement time to identify the specific hardware configuration.
Serial number of the environmental instrument or sensor suite used for capture; use the hardware identifier printed on the device or calibration record.
Depth in meters at which environmental measurements were captured at the site; record the active measurement point for the sensor deployment rather than the sample collection depth if they differ.
Timezone used to timestamp the environmental capture session, recorded to normalize measurements collected across field sites and time windows.
Operational calibration state of the environmental sensor suite at the time of capture; record whether the instrument was calibrated and validated before the field session.
Version or identifier of the field measurement protocol used to collect temperature, pH, salinity, and nutrient data at the reef site.
Role of the person or team operating the field measurement instruments during capture, such as field researcher or sensor technician.

env_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data-artefact properties of the environmental readings: file identity, format, size, dimensions, storage, and technical acquisition quality. I excluded the actual instrument configuration and site-capture settings because those belong to env_site_measurement, and I excluded processed summaries or ecological interpretation because those belong to env_processing and environmental_table. I also avoided repeating sample/site identity fields that belong to coral_reef_sample or capture-session fields already owned by the Capture node. No already_generated list was provided, so there were no explicit duplicates to avoid beyond staying in signal territory.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw environmental readings artifact; use a stable string such as 'ENVRAW_GBR_SITE03_2024_05_17'. This identifies the raw capture output before any cleaning or aggregation.
File format of the raw environmental measurement artifact, recorded as the stored digital representation produced by the capture system.
File size in bytes for the raw environmental data artifact at the point of storage or handoff; used as a technical property of the signal file.
Number of raw measurement rows or records contained in the environmental signal file; record at ingestion to indicate data volume before processing.
Number of columns or measurement fields present in the raw environmental signal file; capture this as a structural property of the artifact before processing.
Storage location or URI for the raw environmental signal file, such as a path in object storage or a repository link. Use a resolvable string like 's3://bucket/path/file.csv'.
Checksum or hash of the raw environmental signal file used for integrity verification during storage and transfer; report the algorithm and digest as a string if available.
Technical quality indicator for the raw environmental signal file, based on completeness, corruption status, or capture integrity at ingest time.

env_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the cleaning, transformation, and assembly parameters used to convert raw environmental readings into a structured site-condition dataset. I excluded the raw file properties because those belong to env_signal, and I excluded the resulting processed table properties because those belong to environmental_table. I also avoided any capture settings or sample identity fields. No already_generated list was supplied, so I only constrained by process semantics and the DAG context.

md_schema.descr: Software package used to clean and assemble raw environmental readings into the site-condition dataset; report the software name used in this workflow.
Software version used for environmental data processing, recorded at the time the raw readings were cleaned and structured.
Code repository, package source, or workflow repository used for environmental processing; provide a URI or repository identifier when applicable.
Version or identifier of the filtering and cleaning rules applied to the raw environmental readings before dataset assembly.
Method used to handle missing environmental observations during processing, such as interpolation, omission, or imputation.
Method used to detect and handle outlier environmental measurements during processing, applied before the structured dataset was generated.
Whether and how environmental measurement units were standardized during processing, for example converting all temperatures to Celsius and salinity to PSU-equivalent reporting.
Number of environmental records retained after cleaning and assembly, measured at the end of processing before the derivative table is created.
Overall technical quality assessment of the environmental processing run, indicating whether the cleaned dataset was successfully assembled for downstream analysis.

environmental_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result properties of the processed environmental table: table identity, dimensions, variable coverage, schema summary, and quality indicators that describe the output of env_processing. I excluded raw capture details and processing parameters because those belong to env_site_measurement and env_processing, respectively. I also avoided repeating any site/sample identifiers from upstream entities. No already_generated list was supplied, so the schema focuses on the derivative output itself and not on upstream provenance fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the processed environmental table derivative; use a stable string such as 'ENV_TABLE_GBR_2024_SITESET'. This identifies the integrated site-condition dataset created from cleaned raw environmental readings.
Number of rows in the processed environmental table, measured on the final derivative output after cleaning and assembly.
Number of columns in the processed environmental table, measured on the final derivative output to describe table shape.
Number of distinct reef sites or sampling locations represented in the processed environmental table; record this on the final integrated dataset.
Number of distinct depth levels represented in the processed environmental table; record this at the derivative output stage to summarize spatial stratification.
List of environmental variables retained in the processed table, such as temperature, pH, salinity, and nutrient metrics; describe the final feature set of the derivative output.
Fraction of expected environmental table entries present after processing, expressed as a value between 0 and 1; use this as a technical quality indicator for the derivative output.
Reference to the upstream processing run or workflow identifier that produced this environmental table derivative, used for provenance tracking of the computed result.
Overall quality assessment of the processed environmental table after integration and cleaning, indicating whether it is fit for downstream community analysis.

amplicon_library_prep.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only library preparation workflow parameters, primer/indexing details, amplification conditions, and process quality indicators that describe how community DNA was converted into a 16S sequencing library. I excluded DNA extract properties because those belong to the community_dna entity, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings or raw read/file properties because those belong to sequencing_capture and raw_reads. No already_generated list was provided, so there were no explicit duplicate-field constraints beyond avoiding reused extraction or sequencing-output fields.

md_schema.descr: Library preparation approach used to convert extracted community DNA into an indexed 16S rRNA gene amplicon library; report the workflow or kit name used in this study.
16S rRNA gene region amplified during library preparation, such as V3-V4 or V4; record the target region chosen for the amplicon workflow.
Primer pair used for 16S amplification during library preparation, recorded as the primer set name or sequence pair designation.
DNA polymerase used during PCR amplification of the 16S target during library preparation.
Number of PCR cycles used during amplicon library preparation; record the amplification cycle count applied to community DNA.
Annealing temperature in degrees Celsius used during PCR amplification for amplicon library preparation.
Indexing or barcoding strategy used to multiplex libraries, such as dual-index or single-index tagging.
Method used to select amplicon library fragment sizes before sequencing, such as bead-based cleanup or gel extraction.
Number of independent library preparation replicates generated from the same community DNA extract, recorded at the library prep step.
Overall technical quality assessment of the prepared indexed 16S library, indicating whether it was suitable for downstream sequencing.

sequencing_library.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included intrinsic properties of the prepared amplicon library itself: identity, indexing/barcode structure, insert characteristics, concentration, and readiness for sequencing. I excluded PCR conditions and library-prep workflow parameters because those belong to amplicon_library_prep, and I excluded sequencer run settings and raw read properties because those belong to sequencing_capture and raw_reads. No already_generated list was provided, so I avoided only obvious semantic duplication with the upstream process and downstream signal nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared 16S sequencing library entity; use a stable string such as 'LIB_GBR_D01_SITE03_S01'. This identifies the library as a discrete material distinct from the source DNA and the raw sequencing reads.
Measured concentration of the prepared amplicon library in nanograms per microliter, assessed after cleanup and prior to loading on the sequencer.
Library molarity in nanomolar units, measured or calculated prior to sequencing to determine loading concentration.
Approximate dominant insert or library fragment size in base pairs for the prepared amplicon library, assessed before sequencing.
Adapter and index structure present on the prepared library, describing how sequencing adapters and sample indexes are arranged on the amplicon molecule.
Index or barcode sequence set used to identify this library during pooled sequencing; record the barcode scheme or identifier applied to the prepared library.
Boolean flag indicating whether the prepared library met internal criteria for pooling and loading on the sequencing instrument.
Storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the prepared sequencing library before sequencing run setup; typical values may be 4 or -20 depending on lab practice.
Operational readiness status of the prepared library at the time it was handed off for sequencing, indicating whether it was acceptable for capture on the sequencer.

sequencing_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the sequencing session and instrument configuration used to read the prepared 16S amplicon library. I excluded raw file properties because those belong to raw_reads, and I excluded sample/library intrinsic properties because those belong to the sequencing_library entity. I also avoided downstream processing and derivative quality metrics beyond capture-run technical status. No already_generated list was supplied, so I focused on non-overlapping capture-level fields and included the required hardware manufacturer/model/serial information.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the sequencing capture session; use a stable string such as 'SEQRUN_MISEQ_2024_05_17_01'. Assigned when the amplicon library is loaded onto the instrument and the run is initiated.
Manufacturer of the high-throughput sequencing instrument used for capture, recorded as the hardware vendor for the sequencer.
Model designation of the sequencing instrument used for capture, recorded at run setup to identify the specific platform configuration.
Serial number of the sequencing instrument used for capture; use the hardware identifier from the device or maintenance record.
Sequencing reagent kit or chemistry used for the run, recorded as the kit name configured for the capture session.
Flow cell or cartridge type used in the sequencing run, recorded as part of the capture configuration.
Configured number of cycles per read in the sequencing run, measured at run setup; typical values depend on the 16S amplicon workflow and platform.
Whether the run was configured for single-end or paired-end capture of the amplicon library.
Date the sequencing capture session was initiated or completed, recorded to link instrument settings with raw data output.
Role of the person or team operating the sequencer during capture, such as sequencing technician or core facility operator.
Calibration or maintenance status of the sequencer at the time of capture, used as a technical indicator of instrument readiness.
Overall technical quality assessment of the sequencing capture session, indicating whether the run was successful enough to generate usable raw 16S data.

raw_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data-artefact properties of the FASTQ reads: file identity, format, size, read counts, read lengths, storage location, integrity checks, and technical run metrics. I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to sequencing_capture, and I excluded trimming, denoising, or any biological interpretation because those belong to read_processing and downstream derivatives. No already_generated list was provided, so I avoided only semantic overlap with the Capture node and downstream Process/Derivative nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw FASTQ read artifact produced by the sequencing run; use a stable string such as 'FASTQ_GBR_MISEQ_2024_05_17_R1'. This identifies the unprocessed sequencing data object.
File format of the raw sequencing reads, typically FASTQ for 16S amplicon sequencing; record the stored digital format of the signal artifact.
File size in bytes of the raw read artifact at storage or handoff time; use this as a technical property of the raw signal file.
Whether the raw sequencing data are stored as single-end or paired-end reads in the raw FASTQ artifact.
Total number of reads contained in the raw FASTQ artifact, measured from the unprocessed sequencing output.
Nominal read length in base pairs for the raw sequencing reads, recorded from the sequencing output before any trimming or filtering.
Storage location or URI for the raw FASTQ file, such as an object-store path or repository link; use a resolvable string like 's3://bucket/path/reads.fastq.gz'.
Checksum or hash of the raw FASTQ artifact used to verify file integrity during storage and transfer; report the algorithm and digest as a string if available.
Percentage of bases in the raw sequencing reads with Phred quality score Q30 or greater, calculated as a technical quality metric for the raw signal file.
Technical flag indicating whether adapter sequence contamination is detected in the raw FASTQ file prior to downstream processing.

read_processing.reasoning: This is still the read_processing Process node, but I removed the colliding generic software fields because they were already generated elsewhere in the DAG. I kept only read-processing-specific parameters and quality indicators that remain within this node's semantic territory: trimming, denoising, chimera removal, merging, retained read count, and run quality. I excluded raw read properties and downstream amplicon feature outputs, and I avoided repeating any previously generated generic processing metadata.

md_schema.descr: Strategy used to trim low-quality bases and adapter/primer sequences from raw reads before denoising and merging.
Number of bases removed from the left end of each read during trimming, measured in base pairs at the processing step.
Number of bases removed from the right end of each read during trimming, measured in base pairs at the processing step.
Forward-read truncation length in base pairs used during processing before denoising or merging.
Reverse-read truncation length in base pairs used during processing before denoising or merging, if paired-end data were used.
Algorithm used to denoise reads and infer high-resolution amplicon variants, such as exact sequence variant inference or OTU clustering.
Method used to identify and remove chimeric reads during processing before the curated amplicon dataset was generated.
Strategy used to merge paired-end reads, if applicable, during processing of the amplicon dataset.
Number of reads retained after trimming, denoising, merging, and filtering; record at the end of the processing step.
Overall technical quality assessment of the read-processing run, indicating whether the curated amplicon dataset was successful and suitable for downstream analysis.

amplicon_features.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result properties of the amplicon feature table: identity, table dimensions, feature/observation counts, sequence representation, and output quality indicators. I excluded raw read properties because those belong to raw_reads, and I excluded processing parameters because those belong to read_processing. Because prior collisions were reported for generic processing software fields, I avoided any reused field ids in that family and used output-specific derivative names instead. No already_generated list was provided, so the schema focuses on the amplicon-feature result itself.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the processed amplicon feature table derivative; use a stable string such as 'AMP_FEATURES_GBR_2024_SITESET'. This identifies the curated microbial feature matrix produced from read processing.
Number of microbial features retained in the amplicon feature table, measured on the final derivative output; features may be ASVs, OTUs, or equivalent sequence variants depending on the workflow.
Number of samples represented as columns or rows in the amplicon feature table, depending on orientation; record this on the final derivative output.
Orientation of the amplicon feature table, indicating whether features are stored by rows or columns in the final output table.
Number of nonzero cells in the amplicon feature table, measured after processing and before downstream analysis; indicates sparsity of the derivative output.
Total summed abundance across all retained amplicon features in the derivative table, recorded at the final output stage.
Format used to store representative feature sequences in the derivative output, such as nucleotide strings or consensus records.
Abundance data type represented in the amplicon feature table, such as counts or relative abundances, recorded for the final derivative.
Overall quality assessment of the amplicon feature derivative, indicating whether the feature table is suitable for downstream ecological analysis.

community_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the analysis workflow, software, and statistical settings used to integrate amplicon features with environmental data. I excluded the feature table and environmental table properties themselves because those belong to upstream Derivative nodes, and I excluded the final interpreted outputs because those belong to community_structure_results. I also avoided the generic processing software field ids that were previously reported as colliding, so I used analysis-specific software identifiers instead. No already_generated list was provided, so the schema is limited to process-level parameters and quality indicators.

md_schema.descr: Software package used to integrate microbial feature profiles with environmental conditions; report the analysis tool name used for this community ecology workflow.
Version of the analysis software used for community integration and association testing, recorded at the time the analysis was run.
Code repository, package source, or workflow repository used for community analysis; provide a URI or repository identifier when applicable.
Community dissimilarity or distance metric used to evaluate spatial heterogeneity among microbial profiles, such as Bray-Curtis or weighted UniFrac.
Ordination or multivariate method used to summarize community structure and environmental relationships, if applied in the integration workflow.
Statistical method used to test associations between microbial features and reef site variables, recorded at the analysis step.
List or description of environmental covariates included in the community analysis model, such as depth, temperature, pH, salinity, and nutrients.
Method used to correct for multiple hypothesis testing in association analyses, if applicable, recorded at the analysis step.
Number of permutations used for resampling-based community analysis tests, measured at the analysis step when relevant.
Overall technical quality assessment of the community analysis run, indicating whether the integrated statistical workflow completed successfully.

community_structure_results.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only the computed result outputs of the community analysis: result identity, dimensionality, diversity/structure summary measures, association summaries, and result quality indicators. I excluded analysis software and statistical parameters because those belong to community_analysis, and I excluded the upstream amplicon and environmental table properties because those belong to their own derivative nodes. No already_generated list was provided, but I avoided reusing process-level field ids and focused on final interpretation-ready outputs.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the integrated community structure results derivative; use a stable string such as 'COMM_RESULTS_GBR_2024_SITESET'. This identifies the final analysis output combining microbial and environmental information.
Number of rows in the community structure results output table or result object, measured on the final derivative artifact.
Number of columns or result fields in the final community structure output, measured on the derivative artifact.
Primary microbial diversity metric reported in the results, such as alpha diversity index or beta diversity summary, used to characterize community structure.
Numerical value of the primary diversity metric reported for the integrated results object; record the summary value corresponding to the final analysis output.
Concise summary of the direction or strength of associations between microbial community structure and reef environmental variables, as represented in the final result.
Number of environmental associations or taxa-environment relationships deemed significant in the final integrated analysis results.
Summary of effect sizes reported for the main community-environment relationships in the final derivative output; use a single representative value or summary statistic when applicable.
URI or file path to a visualization or report artifact generated from the final community structure results, such as ordination plots or summary figures.
Overall quality assessment of the final integrated results object, indicating whether the community structure output is complete and suitable for interpretation.
